tips.text: Never learn "Mutter", always "die Mutter" — German words come with their gender attached, and this drill insists on it.

tips.title: Verb in second position
tips.text: German main clauses put the verb second, whatever comes first: "Ich heiße Anna." / "Aus Spanien komme ich." Both are fine — "Ich aus Spanien komme" is not.

tips.title: Three patterns pay out
tips.text: Ends in -e? Usually die. Ends in -chen? Always das. Male person or -er tool? Usually der. That covers most of tonight's table.

speaking.topic: A betting game about noun genders. Keep it quick and playful; explain the pattern behind every noun I get wrong.

Gender patterns: -e, -chen, -ung, -er
Reacting fast without translating first
speaking.material:
Game rules:
- You are the croupier. Each round, name one German noun from A1 vocabulary (family, café, everyday objects) WITHOUT its article.
- I bet by calling der, die or das.
- Right call = 10 points for me. Wrong = you keep the points and reveal the pattern if there is one (-e mostly die, -chen always das, -er often der…).
- 10 rounds, then convert my points to the final score.

tips.title: Say the ones first
tips.text: German swaps two-digit numbers: 34 is vierunddreißig — "four-and-thirty". Hear the und? The small digit came first.

speaking.topic: Numbers 0–100 out loud and as digits, then simple prices with "Das kostet … Euro". Mix directions: sometimes say the digit, sometimes I do.

The und-swap in 21–99 (einundzwanzig)
Prices: Euro und Cent
speaking.material:
Drill sets:
- Core numbers: 0–12 individually, then 13–19 (-zehn), then the tens (zwanzig, dreißig … hundert).
- The swap rule: 21 = einundzwanzig (one-and-twenty), 45 = fünfundvierzig, 99 = neunundneunzig.
- Prices to ask with "Was kostet das?": 2,50 € · 7 € · 19,90 € · 64 € · 99 Cent.

Answering W-questions in full sentences

speaking.material:
Passage (show it to me exactly like this):
Hallo! Ich heiße Lena und ich komme aus Österreich. Ich wohne jetzt in Hamburg und arbeite als Köchin in einem kleinen Café. Meine Familie ist groß: Ich habe zwei Brüder und eine Schwester. Am Sonntag koche ich für alle — das ist mein Hobby und mein Beruf!

Ask me (one at a time):

2. Wo wohnt sie jetzt?
3. Was ist ihr Beruf?
4. Wie viele Geschwister hat sie?

tips.title: Das ist… / Das sind…
tips.text: One person: "Das ist mein Bruder." Several: "Das sind meine Eltern." The photo-pointing phrase carries the whole story.

speaking.material:
Story skeleton:
- You invent a family photo: 4 people, their names, one detail each (age, job, or mood). Describe it to me slowly, twice if I ask.
- Beat 1: I name who is in the photo (Das ist… / Das sind…).
- Beat 2: I say one thing about each person (Er ist… / Sie hat…).
- Beat 3: I say which person I like and why, very simply.
- Required: sein in er/sie/wir forms, at least 4 family words with the right article.

tips.title: The prefix jumps to the end
tips.text: aufstehen becomes "Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf." The verb goes second, the prefix goes last — everything else sits between.

tips.title: Only der becomes den
tips.text: In the accusative, die, das and the plurals stay put. Only the masculine changes: der→den, ein→einen, kein→keinen. One row of the table does all the work.

speaking.topic: Twelve English sentences that pit accusative forms (den, einen, keinen, ihn) against their nominative lookalikes. Serve them one at a time and be strict about the endings.

Accusative pronouns: mich, dich, ihn, sie, uns

tips.title: halb zehn is 9:30
tips.text: German "halb" looks forward: halb zehn means half an hour BEFORE ten, so 9:30. Check the first sentence twice.

speaking.topic: A short café ordering scene to read and answer questions about. Ask in simple German; two questions make me pull an exact price and an exact time out of the text.
practisePoints: Finding exact prices and times in a text
Understanding kein in context (kein Croissant mehr)
Answering with accusative objects: einen Käsekuchen
speaking.material:
Passage (show it to me exactly like this):
Es ist halb zehn am Samstagmorgen. Paul sitzt im Café Sonne und liest die Karte. Er möchte einen Milchkaffee und ein Croissant. Der Milchkaffee kostet 3,80 Euro, das Croissant kostet 2,20 Euro. Die Kellnerin sagt: "Wir haben leider kein Croissant mehr." Paul nimmt dann einen Käsekuchen. Um zehn Uhr kommt seine Freundin Mia, und sie bestellt nur ein Wasser.

Ask me (one at a time):
1. Wann sitzt Paul im Café?
2. Was möchte Paul zuerst bestellen?
3. Was kostet der Milchkaffee?
4. Warum nimmt Paul einen Käsekuchen?
5. Um wie viel Uhr kommt Mia, und was bestellt sie?

tips.title: Three angles always work
tips.text: Colour, where you buy or eat it, and what you do with it: "Es ist weiß, ich trinke es zum Frühstück." Sold — that's die Milch.

speaking.topic: A taboo guessing game with supermarket items. I describe, you guess. Keep it playful and never let me say the secret word.
practisePoints: Describing food with colours, sizes and simple verbs
Accusative objects in the descriptions
Staying in German when the exact word is missing
speaking.material:
Game rules:
- Give me 8 supermarket items one at a time, in English, e.g. apple, milk, bread, cheese, egg, tomato, butter, chocolate.
- I must describe each item IN GERMAN without saying the German word itself (das runde, rote Obst…), and you guess it.
- You guess it from my German = 10 points for me. I say the secret word or fall into English = 0 points for that round.
- Bonus: +2 points per round if my description uses a correct accusative (Man kauft einen…, Ich esse keinen…).
- 8 rounds, then convert my points to the final score.

tips.text: Negating a noun with ein or no article? Use kein, bent like ein: keinen Saft, keine Butter, kein Ei. nicht negates verbs and adjectives instead.

Story skeleton:

- Beat 4: a happy end of my choosing — a colleague drives me, or the boss is even later.
- Required: at least 3 separable verbs, 2 exact clock times, and one kein-sentence.

tips.title: Six words, always dative
tips.text: mit, nach, bei, von, zu, aus — chant them once a day. After any of the six: dem, der, dem. No exceptions, no mercy.

speaking.topic: Twelve English sentences aimed at dative prepositions and dative verbs. Serve one at a time; the endings dem/der/einem/meiner are what you grade hardest.
practisePoints: mit/nach/bei/von/zu/aus always take the dative
Dative verbs: helfen, gefallen, gehören + dative object
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns
scoringCriteria: the dative verbs built the German way
priorityErrors: gefallen/helfen built with an accusative object
speaking.material:
Sentences to serve one at a time (accept any correct German):
1. She helps her brother.
2. The gift is from my aunt.
3. I'm going to the doctor tomorrow.
4. He lives with his parents.
5. We ride to work with the bus.
6. The jacket belongs to the woman.
7. Berlin pleases me a lot. (gefallen!)
8. After work I go home.
9. She comes from Switzerland.
10. Can you help me, please?
11. I got the book from a friend.
12. The keys belong to him.

help.intro: Hide-and-seek across a German city: your AI hides in a place and describes it in dative clues, then you hide. Every clue is a little grammar test wearing a costume.

tips.title: A clue that scores full
tips.text: "Ich fahre mit dem Zug. Viele Leute stehen bei den Gleisen." Two clean dative phrases — the answer (der Bahnhof) is almost a bonus.

speaking.topic: A guessing game about places in the city, played with dative prepositions. You describe, I guess — then we swap roles.
practisePoints: City-place vocabulary: der Bahnhof, die Apotheke, das Rathaus
Dative phrases with mit/bei/von/zu in descriptions
Guessing and describing in full sentences

speaking.material:
Game rules:
- Round type A (4 rounds): you describe a city place in 2–3 German sentences full of dative phrases ("Ich bin bei einem Arzt… Viele Leute warten mit mir…"), and I guess the place in German.
- Round type B (4 rounds): roles swap — I describe a place with at least two dative phrases and you guess.
- Scoring: each correct guess of mine = 10 points. Each of my descriptions = up to 15 points (5 per correct dative phrase, max 3 counted). Wrong dative endings score 0 for that phrase.
- 8 rounds total, then convert my points to the final score.

tips.text: For question 5, weigh the days: rain and delay, then boat, sun and the best sandwich of her life. "Das Ende war schön" is a perfectly good A2 conclusion.

speaking.topic: A holiday postcard where a few things went wrong. Ask comprehension questions in simple German; the last one is an inference question with no literal answer in the text.
practisePoints: Reading Perfekt forms without stumbling
Answering in the Perfekt about a third person
Drawing a simple conclusion beyond the text

speaking.material:
Passage (show it to me exactly like this):
Liebe Oma,
viele Grüße aus Lübeck! Die Reise hat chaotisch angefangen: Unser Zug ist mit zwei Stunden Verspätung gefahren, und dann hat es den ganzen ersten Tag geregnet. Wir sind trotzdem zur Altstadt gegangen und haben das Holstentor gesehen. Am zweiten Tag ist die Sonne gekommen, und wir sind mit einem kleinen Boot gefahren. Abends habe ich bei einem Fischrestaurant das beste Brötchen meines Lebens gegessen. Ich habe dir eine kleine Überraschung gekauft!
Deine Marie

Ask me (one at a time):

quizzes.title: Tell it: the best trip of your life

help.intro: Your best trip, told properly: four beats, past tense all the way, and travel's little words — mit, zu, bei — holding it together. Invent freely; grammar is the passport.

tips.title: sein-verbs are your movers
tips.text: The travel verbs are exactly the sein-verbs: bin gefahren, bin geflogen, bin angekommen, bin geblieben. Move the plot with them and the required forms take care of themselves.

speaking.topic: I tell the story of the best trip of my life — real or invented — along your beats, entirely in the Perfekt. Ask two follow-up questions at the end, also to be answered in the Perfekt.
practisePoints: Sustained Perfekt narration across four beats
sein-auxiliary verbs woven in naturally
Dative prepositions as the glue of travel stories
scoringCriteria: a story with a real highlight, not a list
speaking.material:
Story skeleton:
- Beat 1: departure — where to, with whom, how travelled.
- Beat 2: arrival and first impression.
- Beat 3: the highlight — the one moment that made the trip.
- Beat 4: return and what I brought back (a thing or a memory).
- Required: at least 6 different Perfekt verbs, 2 of them with sein (ist gefahren / ist geblieben…), and 3 dative-preposition phrases (mit dem Zug, bei meiner Tante, nach einem Tag…).

tips.text: While listening, hunt the participles: gefunden, gefahren, passiert. Get the verbs and the story's skeleton is yours — the details hang off them.

practisePoints: Catching a spoken story without reading it

scoringCriteria: the retelling covers the main events in order
Perfekt forms correct in the retelling
priorityErrors: key events missing from the retelling
speaking.material:
The piece you perform:
- Invent a light 60-second anecdote in simple A2 German, told in the Perfekt: someone's small everyday adventure with a surprise at the end (a lost key found in the fridge, a wrong train that led somewhere nice…). 6–8 short sentences, no vocabulary above A2.
- Tell it to me aloud. I may ask for ONE repetition.
Then:
1. I retell the anecdote in my own words, in the Perfekt.
2. Ask me two detail questions about what happened.
3. Ask me one inference question: why was the surprise a good or bad one for the person?

Dative pronouns: euch, Ihnen, dir
Perfekt memories inside a letter

- Close with a warm goodbye and an invitation to visit you.

- danken/gefallen/helfen each used once, each with a correct dative object (euch, Ihnen, deiner Mutter…).
- At least two Perfekt sentences with correct auxiliaries.

Giving directions with imperatives
Dates and ordinals: am ersten Mai, am zweiten Tag

usable, correct directions in part two

tips.title: Wo = rest, wohin = motion
tips.text: Ask yourself: is anything moving somewhere? No → dative (auf dem Tisch). Yes → accusative (auf den Tisch). The question word tells you before you answer.

speaking.topic: Furniture vocabulary drilled through the two-way prepositions. Alternate two question shapes: "Wo ist die Lampe?" (dative answer) and "Wohin stelle ich die Lampe?" (accusative answer). Re-ask every item I miss, in the other case.
practisePoints: Furniture words with their articles
wo + dative: Die Lampe steht auf dem Tisch
wohin + accusative: Ich stelle die Lampe auf den Tisch

wrong gender making the case invisible
speaking.material:
Words to drill (word = meaning):
der Tisch = table · der Stuhl = chair · der Schrank = wardrobe · der Teppich = carpet · der Spiegel = mirror · das Bett = bed · das Regal = shelf · das Sofa = sofa · das Fenster = window · das Bild = picture · die Lampe = lamp · die Tür = door · die Wand = wall · die Ecke = corner · die Küche = kitchen
Drill shape: mix "Wo…?" questions (answer: auf dem Tisch, an der Wand) with "Wohin…?" questions (answer: auf den Tisch, an die Wand) — same furniture, different case.

help.intro: A memory duel played with furniture: hold the AI's room in your head, rebuild it, then furnish your own. Every sentence is a little case exam with points on the table.

tips.title: Things stand, lie or hang
tips.text: German furniture is picky: der Schrank steht, der Teppich liegt, das Bild hängt. Match the verb to the object's posture and collect the bonus.

speaking.topic: A memory game about room descriptions. You describe your room, I reconstruct it, then I describe mine — and you check my case choice sentence by sentence.
practisePoints: Position verbs: stehen, liegen, hängen
Two-way prepositions with the dative for positions
Holding six facts in memory in German
speaking.material:
Game rules:
- Phase 1: describe your (invented) room in exactly 6 German sentences using two-way prepositions (Das Bett steht an der Wand. Der Teppich liegt unter dem Tisch…). I may hear it twice.
- Phase 2: I reconstruct the positions from memory — one sentence per item. Each correctly remembered position = 5 points; correct case on top = 5 more (max 60).
- Phase 3: I describe MY room in 6 sentences. You check every sentence: right case = 5 points, wrong case = 0 and a one-line correction saved for the report (max 30).
- Bonus 10 points if I use stehen/liegen/hängen correctly at least once each. Convert my points to the final score.

help.intro: Here English stops helping: after weil, dass and wenn, the verb walks to the end of the line. Twelve sentences to break the old order until the new one feels natural.

tips.title: weil sends the verb to the end
tips.text: "Ich bin müde, weil ich schlecht geschlafen habe." Everything after weil queues up, and the verb closes the door. In sentence 12, habe comes dead last — after the participle.

speaking.topic: Twelve English sentences whose word order must be broken on the way into German: weil, dass and wenn kick the verb to the very end of their clause. Serve one at a time and grade the verb position above everything else.
practisePoints: weil/dass/wenn push the verb to the end of the clause
The comma between main and subordinate clause
wenn-first sentences: verb, verb in the middle
scoringCriteria: verb-final position in every subordinate clause
priorityErrors: English word order kept after weil/dass
speaking.material:
Sentences to serve one at a time (accept any correct German):
1. I'm tired because I slept badly.
2. She says that she has no time.
3. We're staying home because it's raining.
4. I think that the film is boring.
5. If the weather is good, we'll go to the park.
6. He's happy because his team won.
7. I know that you can't come.
8. She's learning German because she wants to work in Berlin.
9. If I have time, I'll call you.
10. I hope that the test isn't hard.
11. We're eating early because the restaurant closes at nine.
12. He says that he got up at six. (Perfekt — watch the pile-up!)

tips.title: The plan-saving sentence
tips.text: "Wenn das Museum am Sonntag geschlossen ist, gehen wir stattdessen ins Kino." Condition first, comma, then the rescue — verb right after the comma.

speaking.topic: We plan a weekend together. Create TWO scheduling conflicts I must resolve ("Saturday morning you're busy", "the museum is closed on Sunday") — I should propose alternatives with wenn-clauses ("Wenn du am Samstag arbeitest, gehen wir am Sonntag."). Push for at least one werden-future sentence about the final plan.
practisePoints: wenn-clauses to handle conflicts and conditions
Suggesting and agreeing: Wollen wir…? Wie wäre es mit…?
Futur with werden for the settled plan
scoringCriteria: both conflicts resolved with real alternatives
one clean werden-future about the plan

quizzes.title: Reading: the flat ad & the email

help.intro: Real-life reading: an ad says one thing, an email wants another. Four questions warm you up; the fifth makes you the judge — and every verdict needs a weil.

tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Make a match table in your head
tips.text: Balcony? Light? Price? Cat? Time? Tick each wish against the ad before question 5 — two wishes fail, and they are exactly what your weil-sentences are for.

speaking.topic: Two short texts — a flat-viewing ad and a renter's email — read together. The final question crosses the texts: does the flat fit what the renter wants? Make me justify with weil.
practisePoints: Extracting facts from two related texts
Comparing wishes against reality
Justifying a judgment with weil + verb-final
scoringCriteria: facts pulled correctly from the right text
priorityErrors: question 5 answered from one text only
speaking.material:
Text 1 — the ad (show both texts exactly like this):
Helle 2-Zimmer-Wohnung im 3. Stock, 52 m², Balkon zum Hof. Kleine Küche, neues Bad, kein Aufzug. 5 Minuten zur U-Bahn. 780 Euro kalt. Haustiere sind leider nicht erlaubt. Besichtigung am Samstag um 11 Uhr.

Text 2 — the email:
Guten Tag, ich interessiere mich für Ihre Wohnung. Ich suche etwas Helles mit Balkon, und die U-Bahn ist mir wichtiger als ein Aufzug, weil ich viel arbeite und wenig zu Hause bin. Mein Budget ist maximal 800 Euro kalt. Eine Frage habe ich: Ich habe eine kleine Katze — ist das ein Problem? Am Samstag kann ich leider erst um 14 Uhr. Mit freundlichen Grüßen, J. Weber

Ask me (one at a time):
1. Wie groß ist die Wohnung, und was kostet sie?
2. Was ist Herrn Weber wichtiger als ein Aufzug — und warum?
3. Welche Frage stellt Herr Weber in der E-Mail?
4. Welches Termin-Problem gibt es am Samstag?
5. Passt die Wohnung zu Herrn Weber? Answer with "Ja/Nein/Teilweise, weil…" and use BOTH texts.

tips.title: Pain arrives in the dative
tips.text: German pain happens TO you: "Mir tut der Kopf weh." The head is the subject, you are the dative. Plural aches flip the verb: "Mir tun die Ohren weh."

speaking.topic: You are a calm, friendly doctor, I am the patient. I describe three symptoms (wehtun + dative: Mir tut der Kopf weh…), you give simple advice I must show I understood, and at the end we negotiate a follow-up appointment — you reject my first suggested date so I must propose another.
practisePoints: wehtun + dative: Mir tut der Hals weh / Mir tun die Beine weh
Understanding advice and saying it back
Negotiating a date: Geht es am Donnerstag um zehn?
scoringCriteria: three symptoms with correct wehtun grammar
advice confirmed back in my own words
the appointment negotiated to a real date and time
priorityErrors: wehtun built without the dative (ich tue weh…)

help.intro: Fifteen adjective pairs and their ladders. German never says "more cheap" — it bolts -er onto the word and often adds an umlaut. Then you put the forms to work comparing real things.

tips.title: No "mehr" before adjectives
tips.text: English says "more expensive"; German never does. It is teurer, not "mehr teuer" — every adjective climbs with -er, however long it is.

speaking.topic: Adjective pairs climbed through all three steps — alt, älter, am ältesten — then quick "compare these two things" mini-prompts (a bike and a car, coffee and tea…) where I must build the comparison sentence myself, with als.
practisePoints: Comparative forms incl. umlauts and irregulars
am + -sten for the superlative
Comparing with als: schneller als, lieber als
priorityErrors: mehr + adjective instead of the -er form
speaking.material:
Pairs to drill (base = opposite; climb both where sensible):
alt = jung · groß = klein · schnell = langsam · teuer = billig · warm = kalt · gut = schlecht · viel = wenig · gern = ungern · hoch = niedrig · nah = weit · schön = hässlich · leicht = schwer · laut = leise · früh = spät · stark = schwach
Watch the irregulars: gut/besser/am besten · viel/mehr/am meisten · gern/lieber/am liebsten · hoch/höher/am höchsten · nah/näher/am nächsten — and the umlaut climbers alt/älter, groß/größer, warm/wärmer.

quizzes.title: Tell it: Als ich klein war

help.intro: A story built on a hinge: then and now. Comparatives measure the distance, weil explains it, and "Als ich klein war" opens the door. True stories and invented ones score the same.

tips.title: als once, wenn whenever
tips.text: A single period or moment in the past takes als: "Als ich klein war". Repeated or future events take wenn. Childhood happened once — als it is.

speaking.topic: I tell a then-versus-now story about my childhood along your four beats, contrasting past and present with comparatives and explaining with weil. Ask two follow-up questions at the end.
practisePoints: Als for one-time past periods: Als ich klein war…

weil-clauses giving honest reasons

a real contrast, not two separate lists
speaking.material:
Story skeleton:
- Beat 1: where and how I lived as a child (Als ich klein war, …).
- Beat 2: one thing I loved doing then — and why (weil…).
- Beat 3: how my life is different now — at least 3 comparative sentences (Heute ist meine Wohnung kleiner, aber…).
- Beat 4: one thing that is better today and one that was better then, with a weil for each.
- Required: 3+ comparatives with als, 2+ weil-clauses (verb-final), and the opener "Als ich klein war" used at least once. Invented childhoods welcome.

Passage (show it to me exactly like this):
Anzeige 1 — Café Morgenrot sucht eine freundliche Servicekraft. Sie arbeiten am Wochenende und an drei Abenden pro Woche. Wir bieten ein junges Team und flexible Pausen, aber der Lohn ist nicht hoch. Erfahrung ist nicht nötig.

1. Wann muss man im Café Morgenrot arbeiten?
2. Was bietet das Büro Weber und Partner?

tips.title: Firm content, soft grammar
tips.text: The trick of German complaint mail: state facts hard (Die Heizung ist seit einer Woche kaputt), then request soft (Könnten Sie bitte…). The Konjunktiv is the velvet glove.

speaking.topic: A polite complaint email to a landlord about a broken heater. Grade the text against the rubric in the material, sentence by sentence, and quote my best Konjunktiv II line back to me.

speaking.material:
Writing task:
- Write an email (8–10 sentences) to your landlord: the heating in your cold flat has been broken for a week.
- Describe the problem, say how it affects you, and make two polite requests in Konjunktiv II (Könnten Sie…? Es wäre schön, wenn…).

- Both requests in correct Konjunktiv II (biggest weight).
- At least 5 correct adjective endings.

tips.title: auf = not here yet
tips.text: Ich freue mich AUF das Wochenende (it's coming), ich freue mich ÜBER das Geschenk (it's here). auf points forward, über looks at what you already have.

speaking.topic: Verbs that come welded to a preposition. First drill the pairings both ways, then force me into free sentences about my own life — one per verb, correct case included.

Akkusativ vs Dativ after the preposition
auf vs über with sich freuen (future vs present)

Verb + preposition pairs to drill (pair = meaning):
sich freuen auf + Akk = to look forward to · sich freuen über + Akk = to be pleased about · warten auf + Akk = to wait for · sich ärgern über + Akk = to be annoyed about · sich interessieren für + Akk = to be interested in · denken an + Akk = to think of · träumen von + Dat = to dream of · sich kümmern um + Akk = to take care of · Angst haben vor + Dat = to be afraid of · sich bedanken für + Akk = to thank for · sprechen über + Akk = to talk about · teilnehmen an + Dat = to take part in

tips.title: The third-sentence slide
tips.text: Most learners start with "Ich würde…" and slide into "Ich arbeite…" by sentence three. Hear yourself say a plain present verb? Stop, smile, redo it with würde.

speaking.topic: I narrate one full day in my dream job — entirely hypothetical, entirely in Konjunktiv II. You keep me honest: any indicative main verb gets flagged and the sentence redone.
practisePoints: Sustaining Konjunktiv II across a whole narrative
hätte/wäre woven in among würde-forms
A purpose clause with damit or um…zu
priorityErrors: sliding back into the indicative mid-story
speaking.material:
Story skeleton (walk me through it beat by beat):
- Beat 1: the morning — how I would get to work, when I would start (Ich würde…, ich müsste nicht…).
- Beat 2: the work itself — what I would do, what I would be (Ich wäre…, ich hätte…).
- Beat 3: the people — what my colleagues would be like, one inflected adjective phrase (nette Kollegen, einen geduldigen Chef).
- Beat 4: the evening — why this job would make me happy (one damit or um…zu clause).
- Required forms: würde + infinitive at least 5 times, hätte and wäre at least once each, one damit or um…zu clause.

Konjunktiv II wishes and hypotheticals

tips.title: Sing the vowel families
tips.text: Strong verbs move in choirs: ei → ie (schreiben/schrieb, bleiben/blieb), i/e → a (finden/fand, sprechen/sprach). Learn one family member and you get its siblings for free.

speaking.topic: Strong-verb Präteritum, drilled as a ladder: infinitive up, Präteritum down, both directions, fast. After every 5 verbs, make me build one instant micro-sentence with a form I just drilled.
practisePoints: Strong-verb vowel changes (gehen → ging, nehmen → nahm)
war/hatte/wurde and the modal Präteritum forms
No endings on ich/er in Präteritum (ich ging, not ich ginge)
scoringCriteria: the correct Präteritum form both directions

Perfekt used where Präteritum was asked
speaking.material:
Verb ladder to drill (infinitive = Präteritum, er/sie form):
gehen = ging · kommen = kam · sehen = sah · geben = gab · nehmen = nahm · finden = fand · fahren = fuhr · schreiben = schrieb · lesen = las · sprechen = sprach · essen = aß · trinken = trank · laufen = lief · schlafen = schlief · bleiben = blieb · rufen = rief · treffen = traf · beginnen = begann · verlieren = verlor · wissen = wusste

tips.title: als, not wenn
tips.text: A single completed moment in the past takes als: "Als sie den Keller öffnete…". wenn in the past means "whenever" — every time, not once upon a time.

speaking.topic: You hand me a scrambled Grimm-style story skeleton; I tell it as a flowing modern fairy tale, entirely in Präteritum, opening with "Es war einmal…". Interrupt only for tense slips.
practisePoints: Sustained Präteritum narration
Relative clauses to introduce characters

scoringCriteria: correct Präteritum forms across the tale
at least two correct relative clauses
a coherent story using every skeleton element
speaking.material:
Story skeleton (present it scrambled, I must order it):
- eine junge Programmiererin, die in einem grauen Hochhaus wohnte
- ein sprechender Kaffeeautomat mit einem geheimen Wunsch
- ein Chef, der nie Danke sagte
- eine Reise in den Keller der Firma, wo etwas Seltsames wartete
- ein Tausch: eine Woche Schweigen gegen einen echten Wunsch
- ein Ende, in dem jemand etwas Wichtiges lernte
Required forms:
- Opening: Es war einmal…
- Präteritum throughout (war, hatte, ging, sagte, wusste…).
- At least 2 relative clauses (die Frau, die…; der Automat, den…).
- One als-clause for a single past moment (Als sie den Keller öffnete, …).

tips.title: werden is the engine
tips.text: German passive always runs on werden: "Das Brot wird gebacken" (is baked), "Die Brücke wurde gebaut" (was built). The Partizip waits at the end of the clause.

speaking.topic: Ten active English sentences that must come out as German passive — werden + Partizip II in the present, wurde + Partizip II in the past. Serve one at a time; re-serve my misses.
practisePoints: Present passive: wird + Partizip II
Past passive: wurde + Partizip II
The agent with von + Dativ where the English names one
scoringCriteria: the correct Partizip II at the end
priorityErrors: ist + Partizip used instead of wird/wurde

Sentences to serve one at a time (German passive required):
1. The bridge was built in 1900.
2. German is spoken here.
3. The letter is being written right now.
4. The window was broken yesterday.

help.intro: A tiny local-news mystery: a suitcase, old letters, a happy ending. Read it, answer about it, and for the finale, flip one of its passive sentences back to active.

tips.title: Passive radar
tips.text: Scan for wurde(n) + a participle at the end — that's your passive. To re-activate it, promote the von-phrase (or invent a doer) to subject: "Zwei Beamte packten die Briefe ein."

speaking.topic: A short newspaper item in narrative Präteritum. Keep everything at B1 — no rewording upwards. Question 5 asks me to hunt down a passive sentence and turn it back into an active one.
practisePoints: Reading narrative Präteritum fluently
Spotting passive constructions in real text
Re-activating a passive sentence with the right subject
scoringCriteria: answers in the past tenses of the text
priorityErrors: answering in present tense about past events
speaking.material:
Passage (show it to me exactly like this):
Aufregung im Stadtpark
Am Dienstagmorgen entdeckte eine Joggerin im Stadtpark einen offenen Koffer, der voller alter Briefe war. Sie rief sofort die Polizei, die nach zwanzig Minuten kam. Die Briefe wurden von zwei Beamten vorsichtig eingepackt. Ein Sprecher der Stadt sagte, dass der Koffer wahrscheinlich seit Jahren in einem Gebüsch lag. Die Besitzerin, eine 90-jährige Frau aus dem Viertel, wurde noch am selben Tag gefunden. Sie freute sich sehr, denn die Briefe stammten von ihrem Mann. Der Koffer war vor langer Zeit bei einem Umzug verloren gegangen.

Ask me (one at a time):
1. Was entdeckte die Joggerin, und wo?
2. Wer kam nach zwanzig Minuten?
3. Wie lange lag der Koffer wahrscheinlich im Gebüsch?
4. Warum freute sich die Besitzerin so sehr?
5. Finde einen Passivsatz im Text und mach daraus einen Aktivsatz. (Check my active version carefully.)

tips.title: A clue that works
tips.text: "Hier wird Brot gebacken. Der Teig wird sehr früh am Morgen gemacht." Two clean passives, one obvious Bäcker — that's a full-points round.

speaking.topic: A profession-guessing game played entirely in the passive. First you mime professions in words, I guess; then we swap and you guess mine. Any non-passive clue sentence loses the round.

Profession vocabulary in both directions
Partizip II placed clause-final every time

speaking.material:
Game rules:
- Round type A (4 rounds): you describe a profession using ONLY passive sentences, never naming it — "Hier werden Haare geschnitten. Die Kunden werden gefragt, wie kurz." I guess the profession in German (der Friseur!).
- Round type B (4 rounds): we swap. I describe a profession in passive sentences (at least 2 per round), you guess. If one of my clue sentences is not a correct passive, the round is void.
- Scoring: type A — 10 points per profession I guess right. Type B — 10 points if my passives are correct AND you can guess, +5 bonus for a third correct passive clue.
- 8 rounds total, then convert my points to the final score.

tips.title: deshalb flips, nämlich hides
tips.text: deshalb takes position one and pulls the verb next: "Deshalb zog ich um." nämlich never starts a clause — it tucks in after the verb: "Ich zog um, ich hatte nämlich einen neuen Job."

tips.title: Listen for anchors, not words
tips.text: Grab the five anchors — wer, was, wo, wann, Ergebnis — and let the rest go. A retelling built on five anchors beats a broken word-for-word echo every time.

speaking.topic: You read a 90-second radio-style news miniature aloud (voice mode), normal pace, once — twice only if I ask. Then I retell it in my own words in past tenses, and you check me with three detail questions.

Retelling in Präteritum and Perfekt, not quoting
Holding details for the follow-up questions

speaking.material:
The piece to read aloud (write your own, but it must be):
- A local-news miniature of about 90 seconds / 8–10 sentences, B1 vocabulary only.
- Topic: a small, concrete event — a rescued animal, a reopened bridge, a record-breaking bake sale, a found treasure.
- Written in narrative Präteritum with at least two passive sentences (wurde gerettet, wurde eröffnet…) and one relative clause.
Then:
- I retell the story in my own words (past tenses, not a word-for-word echo).
- Ask me 3 detail questions about facts I did not mention.
- Grade the retelling for coverage and tense control, the questions for accuracy.

help.intro: Bureaucratic German, the fun way: one silly accident, three tense layers. Before, during, damage — each layer has its own grammar, and the rubric checks all three.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: One step further back
tips.text: Plusquamperfekt is the past of the past: hatte/war + Partizip II. "Es hatte geregnet, deshalb war die Straße nass, und dann passierte es." Three layers, three tenses.

speaking.topic: An accident report for an insurance form, written in three tense layers: what had happened before (Plusquamperfekt), what happened (Präteritum), what was damaged (Passiv). Grade it against the rubric, layer by layer.
practisePoints: Plusquamperfekt for the pre-history
Präteritum for the event line
Passive for damage — the classic report voice
scoringCriteria: each tense layer correct and in place
priorityErrors: active sentences in the damage layer
speaking.material:
Writing task:
- Invent a small, harmless household or bicycle accident and write the report (8–10 sentences) for the insurance form.
- Layer 1 — the background: at least 2 sentences in Plusquamperfekt about what had happened before (Ich hatte das Fenster geöffnet…, Es hatte geregnet…).
- Layer 2 — the event: the accident itself in Präteritum.
- Layer 3 — the damage: at least 2 passive sentences (Die Vase wurde zerbrochen. Das Fahrrad wurde beschädigt.).
Rubric (grade against this):
- Each layer present and in its tense (biggest weight).
- Plusquamperfekt formed with hatte/war + Partizip II.
- Sober report style: no du/ihr, no exclamation marks.
- Clear time order, ideally with nachdem or als.

help.intro: You saw everything, officer — now say it precisely. Every person in your statement needs a relative clause, and the officer will keep asking "Welcher Mann genau?" until they get one.

tips.title: The clause case is local
tips.text: The relative pronoun takes its case from its OWN clause: "der Mann, DEN ich sah" (I saw him — accusative), "der Mann, DEM ich half" (I helped him — dative). Ignore the main clause.

speaking.topic: You are a patient, very thorough police officer; I witnessed a silly bicycle incident (nobody hurt, much confusion). Take my statement: what happened, in what order, and exactly WHO was involved — push me to identify every person with a relative clause (der Mann, der…; die Frau, die…; der Junge, den…).
practisePoints: Relative clauses in nominative, accusative and dative
Ordered past narration under questioning
n-declension in action (der Junge → den Jungen)
scoringCriteria: correct relative pronouns for each case
priorityErrors: wrong relative pronoun case (der Mann, den ich half)
der Junge left undeclined (mit der Junge)

help.intro: B2 argument runs on prefabricated steel: a dozen scaffolds that hold any opinion upright. Drill them as chunks until each one assembles itself.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: je…desto is a double comparative
tips.text: "Je mehr Autos fahren, desto schlechter wird die Luft." — comparative on both sides, verb final after je, verb second after desto. Miss one piece and the scaffold collapses.

speaking.topic: Argumentation scaffolds drilled as whole chunks: you state a bare claim, then assign me one scaffold, and I must re-express the claim through it — grammar intact, meaning preserved.
practisePoints: Scaffold chunks recalled verbatim
dass-clauses and ob-clauses with verb-final order
je…desto with the comparative on both sides
speaking.material:
Scaffolds to drill (chunk = meaning):
einerseits … andererseits = on the one hand … on the other · es lässt sich nicht leugnen, dass … = it cannot be denied that · man muss bedenken, dass … = one has to consider that · im Gegensatz dazu = in contrast to that · daraus folgt, dass … = it follows that · ein weiteres Argument dafür ist … = a further argument for it is · dagegen spricht, dass … = against it speaks the fact that · zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen, dass … = in summary one can say · es kommt darauf an, ob … = it depends on whether · ich gebe zu, dass …, dennoch … = I admit that …, nevertheless · je mehr …, desto … = the more …, the more · folglich = consequently
Drill: serve a bare claim (Hausaufgaben sind sinnvoll. / E-Autos lösen alle Probleme.) plus one scaffold; I rebuild the claim through the scaffold. Reject broken word order instantly.

help.intro: Your first editorial: the author never says "I think", yet takes a clear side. Read between the lines, then bend one quote into proper reported speech.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Stance hides in connectors
tips.text: gewiss…dennoch, folglich, doch — these little words carry the author's verdict. Track where each "but" lands and you have the opinion without a single "ich finde".

speaking.topic: A newspaper editorial on e-scooters, locked at B2 — do not simplify or reword it. The questions target the author's stance between the lines, and one asks me to transform a quote into reported speech with Konjunktiv I.
practisePoints: Reading for stance, not just facts
Decoding je…desto and dennoch/folglich logic
Transforming quotes into Konjunktiv I
scoringCriteria: evidence from the text for each answer
priorityErrors: indicative kept in the reported-speech task
stance question answered with surface facts only
speaking.material:
Passage (show it to me exactly like this):
Stolperfallen auf Rädern
Seit fünf Jahren gehören E-Scooter zum Stadtbild, und noch immer wird über sie gestritten. Die Anbieter betonen gern, ihre Fahrzeuge seien ein Baustein der Verkehrswende. Das lässt sich hören — doch wer morgens über kreuz und quer abgestellte Roller steigen muss, dem erscheint diese Verkehrswende eher als Hindernislauf. Die steigenden Unfallzahlen sprechen eine deutliche Sprache: Allein im letzten Jahr wurden in deutschen Großstädten über 9000 Verletzte registriert. Gewiss, das Auto bleibt das größere Problem, und ein Verbot wäre folglich der falsche Weg. Dennoch muss der Wildwuchs geordnet werden: feste Abstellzonen, weniger Lizenzen, klare Regeln. Je verbindlicher die Vorgaben, desto eher wird aus dem Ärgernis ein nützliches Verkehrsmittel. Die Städte sollten das nicht länger den Anbietern überlassen.

Ask me (one at a time):
1. Welche zwei Seiten des Streits nennt der Text?
2. Was hält die Autorin von einem Verbot — und woran erkennt man das?
3. Welche konkreten Maßnahmen werden gefordert?
4. Was bedeutet der je…desto-Satz im Text, in eigenen Worten?
5. Forme dieses Zitat in indirekte Rede mit Konjunktiv I um: "Die Anbieter sagen: Unsere Fahrzeuge sind ein Baustein der Verkehrswende." (Check my Konjunktiv I carefully.)

help.intro: The journalist's tense: what others said, held at arm's length. Ten sentences, and two of them secretly test whether you know when Konjunktiv I must give way to Konjunktiv II.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Fall back only on a collision
tips.text: Use K I first: er sei, er habe, er komme. Only when the K I form looks identical to the indicative (sie kommen, sie haben) do you switch to K II: sie kämen, sie hätten.

speaking.topic: Ten English reported-speech sentences into German indirekte Rede with Konjunktiv I — falling back to Konjunktiv II exactly where K I matches the indicative. Serve one at a time; explain every fallback I miss.
practisePoints: Konjunktiv I forms: er sei, er habe, er wisse, er komme
K II fallback when K I equals the indicative (sie kämen, sie hätten)
Past reported speech: er habe gesehen, sie sei gewesen
priorityErrors: K II used where K I is distinct and required
speaking.material:
Sentences to serve one at a time (Konjunktiv I required, K II only as the correct fallback):
1. She said that she was tired.
2. He said that he had no time.
3. The minister said that the plan was working.
4. She said that they were coming tomorrow. (fallback!)
5. He claimed that he knew nothing about it.
6. The newspaper wrote that prices were rising.
7. She said that she had seen the film.
8. They said that they had (i.e. hätten) no money. (fallback!)
9. He said that he would call later.
10. The spokesperson said that the problem must be solved.

help.intro: You don't get to pick your side — the anti position is yours, defend it. Two rounds of argument and rebuttal, with one je…desto sentence as the price of admission.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Concede, then strike
tips.text: "Zwar ist die Luft ein Problem, dennoch sind viele Menschen auf das Auto angewiesen." Conceding one point first makes your counter-punch twice as credible — and it's pure B2.

speaking.topic: A structured debate on "Autos raus aus den Innenstädten" — and I have drawn the ANTI position (against banning cars), whatever my real view. Two full rounds: I argue, you rebut, I counter your rebuttal. Somewhere in the debate I must land at least one correct je…desto sentence — remind me at the end if it never came.
practisePoints: Building a pro/contra argument in rounds
Concessive moves: zwar…, dennoch…; ich gebe zu, dass…
One mandatory je…desto sentence
scoringCriteria: coherent arguments held across two rounds

help.intro: Six headlines on the table, some of them bluffing. Interrogate the dealer in reported speech — distance is the whole game — then call the bluff and say why.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Konjunktiv I = raised eyebrow
tips.text: "Die Zeitung schreibe, die Preise seien gefallen" — the -e and sei signal "so they claim, I'm not vouching for it". That grammatical eyebrow is exactly what this game trains.

speaking.topic: A fake-news poker game. You deal headlines, I interrogate you in reported speech, then bet fake or real — with a justification.
practisePoints: Reported speech under game pressure (schreibe, behaupte, sei)
Probing questions about sources and numbers
Justifying a verdict with consecutive connectors
scoringCriteria: correct Konjunktiv I when citing the headlines
speaking.material:
Game rules:
- You invent 6 plausible German news headlines; make 2–3 of them subtly fake (wrong detail, invented statistic, absurd cause). Show them numbered.
- For each headline I ask you 1–2 probing questions, and I must refer to the claim in reported speech: "Die Zeitung schreibe, dass…", "Der Artikel behaupte, die Zahl sei gestiegen…". You answer in character as the dealer, giving hints.
- Then I call FAKE or ECHT with one justification sentence (dennoch, folglich, daraus folgt…).
- Scoring: 10 points per correct call, +5 if my interrogation used correct Konjunktiv I, -5 if I slip into the indicative when reporting the claim.
- 6 headlines, then convert my points to the final score.

help.intro: Answer the editorial in its own arena: 120 words to the editor. A thesis, two arguments, one gracious concession — and the author's claims quoted at Konjunktiv distance.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: The concession is the crown
tips.text: B2 examiners look for the concession first: "Zwar hat die Autorin recht, dass…, dennoch übersieht sie…". One honest zwar…dennoch lifts the whole letter a level.

speaking.topic: A letter to the editor responding to the e-scooter editorial "Stolperfallen auf Rädern" (feste Abstellzonen, weniger Lizenzen, kein Verbot). Grade my letter against the rubric, paragraph by paragraph.
practisePoints: Thesis–argument–concession architecture
Reported reference to a source text
Formal letter register at B2
priorityErrors: opinion piled up without a concession
indicative in the reference to the editorial
speaking.material:
Writing task:
- Write a Leserbrief of about 120 words reacting to the editorial's demands (fixed parking zones, fewer licences, no ban). Agree, disagree or differentiate — but take a position.
- Structure: a clear thesis, two supporting arguments, and one concession to the other side (zwar…, dennoch…).
- Refer to the editorial at least once in reported speech (Die Autorin schreibe/fordere, dass…).
- Formal frame: Sehr geehrte Redaktion, … Mit freundlichen Grüßen.
Rubric (grade against this):
- Thesis + 2 arguments + 1 concession all present (biggest weight).
- Correct Konjunktiv I in the reference to the editorial.
- Connectors doing real work (dennoch, folglich, außerdem).
- Around 120 words; formal register throughout.

help.intro: Two minutes of expert opinion, then your colleague asks what was said — and you must retell all of it at reported-speech distance. The Konjunktiv marathon of this module.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Anchor on the verbs of saying
tips.text: Re-launch the Konjunktiv every few sentences: er habe betont, er habe gefordert, er habe gewarnt. Each verb of saying resets your grammar so the indicative can't sneak back in.

speaking.topic: You deliver a 2-minute panel statement aloud (voice mode), in character as an expert. Afterwards I report the whole statement to an absent "colleague" — entirely in reported speech, Konjunktiv I with correct fallbacks, never quoting directly.
practisePoints: Holding a 2-minute spoken argument in memory
Sustained Konjunktiv I across a long report
Reporting modals and passives (die Dächer müssten gebaut werden)
scoringCriteria: the statement's key points all reported
Konjunktiv I sustained with correct fallbacks
no direct quotation in the indicative
priorityErrors: the statistic or demand dropped from the report
speaking.material:
The piece to deliver aloud (write your own, but it must be):
- A 2-minute panel statement (10–12 sentences) by a fictional expert on a climate-and-city topic: e.g. "Solardächer für alle Neubauten" or "Die autofreie Innenstadt bis 2035".
- B2 language: at least one passive with a modal (muss gebaut werden), one statistic (der Anteil, die Mehrheit), one je…desto sentence, and a clear demand at the end.
Then:
- Play my colleague who missed the panel and asks: "Was hat er gesagt?" I report the statement in indirekte Rede — er habe gesagt, die Dächer müssten…, der Anteil sei…
- Interrupt once with "Wirklich? Sagte er das genau so?" and check that I keep the Konjunktiv while confirming.
- Grade coverage of the statement and the reported-speech grammar; direct quotes in the indicative cost points.

help.intro: Numbers you can talk about: rises, falls, shares and majorities, drilled in both directions. The trap the whole drill circles is tiny — auf or um.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: auf lands, um travels
tips.text: stieg AUF 35 Prozent = where it landed; stieg UM 15 Prozentpunkte = how far it travelled. Same climb, two prepositions — pick by what your number describes.

speaking.topic: Statistics language, both directions: you give numbers and I verbalize the trend; then you describe a trend in words and I reconstruct the numbers. Push for variety — no verb twice in a row.
practisePoints: steigen/sinken auf (endpoint) vs um (difference)
Approximation words: knapp, gut, rund
Interpreting numbers with folglich and je…desto
scoringCriteria: varied verbs and chunks across items
priorityErrors: auf/um swapped after steigen and sinken
the same trend verb recycled every item
speaking.material:
Chunks to drill (chunk = meaning):
der Anteil = the share, proportion · die Mehrheit = the majority · die Minderheit = the minority · knapp = just under · gut = a good, just over · rund = around · steigen auf/um = to rise to/by · sinken auf/um = to fall to/by · sich verdoppeln = to double · sich halbieren = to halve · stagnieren = to stagnate · jeder Dritte = one in three · im Vergleich zu = compared to · der Rückgang = the decline · die Zunahme = the increase
Direction 1: you give raw numbers ("2015: 20 Prozent, 2025: 35 Prozent"), I verbalize: "Der Anteil stieg von 20 auf 35 Prozent" — watch my auf vs um!
Direction 2: you say a trend sentence ("Die Zahl hat sich verdoppelt, auf rund 600"), I reconstruct the numbers ("also von etwa 300 auf 600").
Twist: every third item, I must add one je…desto or folglich comment interpreting the number.

help.intro: Tonight you hold the microphone — and your guest is a handful. Summarize, challenge, keep control: the moderator's Konjunktiv keeps you neutral while dennoch keeps you in charge.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: The moderator's move
tips.text: "Sie sagen also, die Regeln seien überflüssig — dennoch zeigen die Zahlen etwas anderes. Wie erklären Sie das?" Summary, distance, challenge: one sentence, full control.

speaking.topic: A live talk-show: you are a provocative, interrupting guest with strong opinions on city traffic; I am the moderator. My job: summarize your points in reported speech, challenge the weak ones, and keep order politely but firmly — with dennoch and folglich doing the steering. Escalate twice; never break character.
practisePoints: Summarizing live speech: Sie sagen also, es gebe…
Firm-but-polite moderation (Moment bitte, dennoch…)
Challenging with folglich and counter-questions
scoringCriteria: accurate reported-speech summaries of the guest
order kept without rudeness or surrender
priorityErrors: summaries in the indicative (taking the guest's side)
losing the moderator role under provocation

help.intro: The module gate, with a twist: defend your drawn side for four exchanges, then switch sides on command and beat your own arguments. Pass it and B2.2 unlocks; your best score counts.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Turn the switch into a weapon
tips.text: Open the second half by reporting yourself: "Vorhin habe ich gesagt, die Kosten seien zu hoch — aber dieses Argument greift zu kurz, denn…". Self-quotation in Konjunktiv I is exactly what the examiners want to hear.

speaking.topic: The closing exam of the module: you draw a debatable thesis and assign me a side at random. I defend it for four full exchanges with structured arguments — then, on your command "Seitenwechsel!", I must argue the opposite side just as convincingly, reporting my own earlier arguments in Konjunktiv I before dismantling them.
practisePoints: Structured argument under an assigned position
Reporting earlier arguments in Konjunktiv I
Passive with modals (das müsse geregelt werden)
Connector logic: dennoch, folglich, je…desto
scoringCriteria: correct Konjunktiv I when reporting the first half
connectors used with correct logic and word order
priorityErrors: Konjunktiv I forms wrong or avoided
connectors with reversed logic (folglich for contrast)

help.intro: B2.2 opens with the genitive in its natural habitat: formal frames. Drill fifteen of them, then build your own — this is the register of emails and contracts.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: des + -s, der without
tips.text: Masculine and neuter genitive add -s to the noun: trotz des Wetters, während des Praktikums. Feminine and plural take der: aufgrund der Verspätung — no ending on the noun.

tips.title: Spoken German cheats — you don't
tips.text: On the street you'll hear "wegen dem Wetter". In formal writing and in this drill, the genitive is the only right answer.

speaking.topic: Formal frames with genitive prepositions: drill the 15 frames in the material, then push me into free production — I must build my own sentence for each preposition, work context preferred.
practisePoints: Genitive endings: des -(e)s for masculine/neuter, der for feminine
Choosing the right preposition for cause, time and concession
Free production in a formal work register
scoringCriteria: the right preposition for the meaning
speaking.material:
Frames to drill (frame = meaning):
trotz des schlechten Wetters = despite the bad weather · trotz aller Bemühungen = despite all efforts · während der Besprechung = during the meeting · während des Praktikums = during the internship · aufgrund der Verspätung = because of the delay · aufgrund technischer Probleme = due to technical problems · infolge des Streiks = as a result of the strike · infolge eines Missverständnisses = as a result of a misunderstanding · wegen des hohen Preises = because of the high price · anlässlich des Jubiläums = on the occasion of the anniversary · anstelle einer Gehaltserhöhung = instead of a pay rise · innerhalb der Frist = within the deadline · außerhalb der Öffnungszeiten = outside opening hours · angesichts der Lage = in view of the situation · mithilfe eines Kollegen = with the help of a colleague

quizzes.title: That's not how I'd have done it

help.intro: The AI tells you four questionable decisions; you say what should have happened instead. Judging the past politely is what the irreal past is for.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Modal at the very end
tips.text: With a modal, the participle becomes an infinitive and the modal goes last: "Er hätte vorher fragen sollen." Never "hätte gefragt sollen".

tips.title: The judge's opening line
tips.text: "An seiner Stelle hätte ich zuerst mit dem Chef gesprochen." — position, hätte, action, participle. One template carries all four stories.

speaking.topic: "Das hätte ich anders gemacht": tell me 4 short decision stories, one at a time — a colleague who quit by text message, a friend who bought a car without a test drive, a boss who cancelled a project by email, a neighbour who sold his flat below value. After each, I evaluate the decision in the irreal past: what the person should, could or would have done. Push back once per story so I have to defend my judgement.
practisePoints: hätte + Partizip II for irreal past (hätte gefragt)
Irreal past with modals: hätte fragen sollen / können / müssen
wäre + Partizip II where the verb takes sein (wäre gegangen)
Softening judgement: An seiner Stelle hätte ich…
scoringCriteria: a real evaluation, not just a summary
priorityErrors: hätte gesollt instead of hätte … sollen

help.intro: German loves folding a whole relative clause into an adjective slot. This drill teaches both moves: packing English clauses in, and unpacking the German monsters again.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: Done = Partizip II, happening = Partizip I
tips.text: Was developed → der entwickelte Plan (Partizip II). Is rising → die steigenden Preise (Partizip I). Decide the time first, the ending second.

tips.title: The full stack
tips.text: "der von der Firma im letzten Jahr entwickelte Plan" — agent, time, participle, noun. Everything between article and noun belongs to the participle.

speaking.topic: Participle workshop in two directions: I turn 8 English relative-clause sentences into German Partizipialattribute, then you give me my German versions back and I unpack them into relative clauses. Serve one at a time and correct immediately.
practisePoints: Partizip II attributes for passive meaning (der entwickelte Plan)
Partizip I attributes for ongoing meaning (die steigenden Preise)
zu + Partizip I for necessity (die noch zu prüfenden Dokumente)
Adjective endings on the participle
priorityErrors: wrong adjective ending on the participle
Partizip I where the meaning is passive
speaking.material:
Sentences to serve one at a time (target: a participial attribute, e.g. "der von der Firma entwickelte Plan"):
1. The plan that was developed by the company failed.
2. The email that was sent yesterday contains an error.
3. The colleague who was hired last month is already leaving.
4. The contract that was signed by both sides is valid.
5. The questions that were discussed in the meeting remain open.
6. The rising prices worry the customers.
7. The documents that are still to be checked are on my desk.
8. The offer that was rejected by the boss was actually good.
Round 2: read my German attributes back to me; I unpack each into a relative clause (der Plan, der von der Firma entwickelt wurde).

help.intro: Contract German is its own dialect: ist zu zahlen, bedarf der Zustimmung. Read a rental excerpt like a tenant who can't afford to misunderstand it.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: ist zu zahlen = must be paid
tips.text: sein + zu + infinitive in contracts means obligation: "Die Miete ist zu zahlen" — the tenant MUST pay. It is never a suggestion.

tips.title: Swap the preposition, keep the meaning
tips.text: trotz + noun phrase and obwohl + full clause say the same thing: "trotz mehrfacher Aufforderung" = "obwohl er mehrfach aufgefordert wurde".

speaking.topic: A simplified rental-contract excerpt plus a short cover letter to read and answer questions about. Ask the questions in German, one at a time; question 5 demands a trotz/aufgrund paraphrase.
practisePoints: Decoding contract prose: ist zu zahlen, bedarf + Genitiv
Participial attributes inside legal sentences
Paraphrasing between trotz + Genitiv and obwohl clauses
priorityErrors: misreading ist zu zahlen as optional
speaking.material:
Passage (show it to me exactly like this):
Auszug aus dem Mietvertrag, § 4 und § 7:
Die monatliche Miete ist bis zum dritten Werktag eines Monats im Voraus zu zahlen. Der Mieter verpflichtet sich, die von ihm verursachten Schäden unverzüglich zu melden. Während der Heizperiode ist eine Mindesttemperatur von 18 Grad zu gewährleisten. Kleinreparaturen bis zu einem Betrag von 100 Euro trägt der Mieter. Trotz mehrfacher Aufforderung nicht gemeldete Mängel gehen zu Lasten des Mieters. Eine Untervermietung bedarf der schriftlichen Zustimmung des Vermieters.

Begleitschreiben der Hausverwaltung:
Sehr geehrter Herr Krause, aufgrund der gestiegenen Nebenkosten erhöht sich Ihre monatliche Vorauszahlung ab dem 1. März um 40 Euro. Infolge der im letzten Jahr durchgeführten Sanierung bleibt die Kaltmiete jedoch unverändert. Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Ihre Hausverwaltung.

Ask me (one at a time):
1. Bis wann muss die Miete gezahlt werden?
2. Welche Pflichten hat der Mieter bei Schäden und Mängeln?
3. Was braucht der Mieter, wenn er untervermieten will?
4. Warum steigt die Vorauszahlung — und warum die Kaltmiete nicht?
5. Formuliere den letzten Satz des Schreibens neu: einmal mit "trotz", einmal mit "obwohl".

help.intro: Modal particles are the seasoning of spoken German — the same sentence, a different feeling. Play twelve rounds of guessing and producing that feeling.

tips.title: How this course works
tips.text: Copy the exercise into your AI assistant (voice mode is best), do the exercise there, and paste the score it gives you back here. Stay with one assistant so your scores stay comparable.

tips.title: doch pushes, halt shrugs
tips.text: "Komm doch!" leans toward you — do come! "Komm halt!" shrugs — come if you must. One word flips the whole invitation.

tips.title: Particles are whispered
tips.text: A real modal particle is never stressed. If you can shout the word ("Das ist JA falsch!"), it has become a normal adverb and means something else.

speaking.topic: A mood-guessing game about modal particles (doch, ja, eben, halt, mal, schon). Keep it playful and always explain the flavour a particle adds.
practisePoints: Hearing the mood a particle adds to an identical sentence
Producing doch, ja, eben, halt in fitting situations
Particle position: after the verb and pronouns, unstressed
scoringCriteria: particles that transport the intended mood in round 2
priorityErrors: stressing the particle like a content word
eben/halt used for urging instead of resignation
speaking.material:
Game rules:
- Round 1 (6 rounds, you serve): say the SAME base sentence with different particles, e.g. "Komm doch!" vs "Komm halt!" vs "Komm schon!". I name the speaker's mood or attitude (encouraging, resigned, impatient…). Right = 10 points; wrong = 0 and you explain the particle's flavour.
- Round 2 (6 rounds, I serve): you give me a situation and a mood ("your friend is late again — resigned"), I produce a sentence with a fitting particle. You guess my intended mood from my sentence. If you guess right, I earn 10 points — my particle did its job.
- Flavour cheat-sheet: doch = friendly urging or contradiction · ja = shared knowledge ("as we both know") · eben/halt = resigned "that's just how it is" · mal = casual softener · schon = reassuring or impatient, context decides.
- 12 rounds total, then convert my points to the final score.

help.intro: The classic B2 writing task: a job application. Your AI invents the ad, you write the email — formal from subject line to signature.

tips.title: How this course works

tips.title: Nominal style, ready to use
tips.text: "Nach Abschluss meines Studiums" beats "Nachdem ich mein Studium abgeschlossen habe" in a letter — shorter, colder, more professional. Two of these lift the whole email.

tips.title: No comma-Sie traps
tips.text: After "Sehr geehrte Frau Weber," the next line starts LOWER case unless it opens with a noun or Sie: "…Weber, mit großem Interesse habe ich…".

practisePoints: Formal correspondence formulas (Sehr geehrte…, Mit freundlichen Grüßen)
Nominal-style phrases in application prose
Genitive and participial attributes under register pressure
scoringCriteria: all required forms present and correct

speaking.material:
Writing task:
- Invent a job ad for my dream job (2 lines) and show it to me.
- I write a formal application email of about 120 words: subject line, formal salutation, why I am applying, two qualifications with evidence, availability, formal closing.
Required forms:
- Full formal register (Sie throughout, no colloquialisms).
- At least 2 nominal-style phrases (nach Abschluss meines Studiums, bei Interesse an meiner Bewerbung…).
- At least 1 genitive preposition and 1 participial attribute (die in der Anzeige genannten Anforderungen).
Rubric (grade against this):
- Register: consistently formal, correct salutation and closing.
- Structure: subject, opening, body, availability, closing.
- The required forms are present and correct.
- Accuracy: case endings, verb position in subclauses.

help.intro: Tell the same story twice: once as it happened, once as the disaster it nearly was. The grammar of relief is the irreal past — enjoy it.

tips.title: The pivot sentence
tips.text: "Und jetzt stellt euch vor, was passiert wäre…" — this line switches the whole story from Perfekt into hätte/wäre land. Say it, then stay there.

tips.title: Hätte first = no wenn needed
tips.text: "Hätte ich das Handy nicht gehört, hätte ich den Flug verpasst." Verb-first replaces wenn and sounds more dramatic — perfect for a near-catastrophe.

speaking.topic: "Beinahe-Katastrophe": I tell a near-miss story twice — first what actually happened, then the replay of what WOULD have happened if things had gone wrong. Interrupt only between the two versions.
practisePoints: Perfekt/Präteritum for the real version
hätte/wäre + participle for the replay, incl. modals
Verb-first irreal conditionals (Hätte ich nicht aufgepasst, …)
scoringCriteria: clean tense separation between the two versions
five correct irreal-past forms, two with modals
a story that actually builds tension
speaking.material:
Story skeleton:
- I invent (or remember) a near-miss: almost missed flight, almost sent the email to the wrong boss, almost signed the wrong contract.
- Version 1 (real events, Perfekt/Präteritum): setup, the moment it almost went wrong, the rescue, the relieved ending.
- Version 2 (the dark replay, irreal past): what would have happened — wäre … gewesen, hätte … verloren, hätte … zahlen müssen. At least 5 irreal-past forms, at least 2 with a modal.
- Closing beat: one lesson drawn, with a genitive preposition (aufgrund dieser Erfahrung…).
- Required: clear tense contrast between the versions; wenn-clause or verb-first conditional (Hätte ich nicht…, dann…).

tips.title: Concede AND advance
tips.text: "Ich verstehe die schwierige Lage. Dennoch habe ich im letzten Jahr zwei Projekte geleitet." — one breath of understanding, then straight back to your case.

tips.title: Courtesy is Konjunktiv
tips.text: "Ich will mehr Geld" gets you shown the door. "Ich hätte gern über mein Gehalt gesprochen" gets you a meeting. Same wish, different mood.

speaking.topic: Salary negotiation: you are my budget-shy boss ("schwierige Marktlage", "vielleicht nächstes Jahr"), I ask for a raise. I use concessions and Konjunktiv II courtesy, but I am not allowed to fold more than twice — if I give in a third time, say so and end the scene. Make me earn every euro.
practisePoints: Konjunktiv II courtesy: Ich hätte gern…, Wäre es möglich…
Concessions that hold ground: Ich verstehe das, dennoch…
Genitive frames under pressure: angesichts meiner Leistungen
Naming achievements concretely, not vaguely

tips.title: Note who, what, when
tips.text: Three messages overload memory fast. Jot one line per voicemail — sender, request, deadline — and the retell builds itself.

tips.title: Hindsight, step by step
tips.text: "Am Montag hätte ich sofort den Lieferanten anrufen sollen." Day, hätte, action, modal at the end — repeat the template for each step.

speaking.topic: A voicemail chain to untangle: you speak three short voicemails aloud, then I summarize the whole situation and say what should have been done at each step — irreal past required.
practisePoints: Catching who wants what from spoken messages
Ordering events with connectors (daraufhin, schließlich)
hätte … sollen/müssen for step-by-step hindsight

a plausible, formal plan for the boss

speaking.material:
The piece (perform each voicemail aloud, natural pace, clearly separated; repeat once on request):
- Voicemail 1, Montag, Kollegin Yildiz: the delivery for the trade fair has not arrived; she asks me to call the supplier before noon.
- Voicemail 2, Dienstag, the supplier: they tried to reach me, the goods are waiting at the depot because nobody confirmed the address; without confirmation today, delivery slips a week.
- Voicemail 3, Mittwoch, the boss: the fair stand has no products, the situation is embarrassing, he expects an explanation and a plan by tomorrow morning.

Then ask me to:
1. Summarize the whole chain in order (Zuerst…, daraufhin…, schließlich…).
2. Say what should have been done at each step (Ich hätte sofort anrufen sollen…, Man hätte die Adresse bestätigen müssen…).
3. Propose the plan for the boss in two sentences, formal register.

tips.title: The three B2.2 flags
tips.text: The examiner listens hardest for: hätte … machen sollen with the modal last, genitive after trotz/aufgrund, and zero du in formal passages. Guard those three.

tips.title: Buy time formally
tips.text: "Das ist eine berechtigte Frage — lassen Sie mich kurz überlegen." Formal filler keeps the register while your brain builds the sentence.

Walk me through a job-interview question, a project post-mortem (what went wrong, what should have been done), a formal clarification call, and a short contract clause I must explain in my own words. Switch scenarios without warning; stay strictly formal except one deliberately casual aside I must handle.

Genitive prepositions and forms in formal speech
Register control: formal by default, no slips
Participial attributes understood and produced
